title: Variant Fallback Bridge Coordinator: cross-environment rollback & reconciliation micro-playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
When a model rollout introduces quality regressions that surface differently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments, our current remediation patterns require manual coordination across routing, KV cache state, and tenant slices. This ticket scopes an operationally-automated "Variant Fallback Bridge" coordinator: a control-plane orchestration that (1) detects variant-level regressions, (2) executes staged fallback across environments with tenant-aware policies, and (3) orchestrates KV-cache reconciliation and post-rollback validation. The deliverable is a micro-playbook plus an automation prototype (feature-flagged) that combines routing rules, targeted tenant quarantines, cache TTL adjustments, and communication templates for customers and account teams.

Why this is different:
- Focus on cross-environment reconciliation rather than simple traffic rollback: we must address sticky state (KV caches, prefix caching, pinned tokens) that cause tenants to continue seeing regressions after traffic is switched.
- Tenant-aware choreography: supports slicing so high-value tenants can be fast-rolled back with minimal impact while allowing staggered rollforward tests for lower-risk tenants.
- Small, automatable building blocks: the coordinator emits explicit steps and idempotent actions (pause-proxy, route-pin, cache-expire, model-unpin) to avoid brittle manual runbooks.

Scope & out-of-scope:
In scope: detection triggers, coordinator state machine, routing API extensions, cache reconciliation actions (TTL bump, prefix invalidation), tenant communication templates, PRs for console hooks, an automated smoke validation pipeline.
Out of scope: major refactor of serving runtime internals, long-lived tenant migrations, changes to private on-prem upgrade windows (coordination only).

Risks & trade-offs:
- Aggressive cache invalidation reduces correctness windows but increases request cost and temporary latency spikes.
- Tenant slicing introduces operational complexity for smaller rollouts; must be guarded by feature flags.
- Rollback automation could inadvertently route traffic to incompatible variants if model-compatibility metadata is stale; mitigation is adding a compatibility check step.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator can execute a staged fallback workflow (global -> regional -> tenant-slice) via an API call
KV cache reconciliation actions are performed as idempotent steps and logged in audit trail
Automated smoke tests confirm baseline QPS and sample output correctness within 10 minutes of rollback for at least one tenant slice
Console shows a single-page runbook view with live step status and links to related alerts/PRs
Customer-facing notification template is generated and can be sent by SRE/CS within 15 minutes of initiating an automated rollback
decisions: Use 'pause-proxy' intermediate action that drains in-flight KV cache tokens before switching routing (reduces sticky-cache fallout)
Implement compatibility check that compares model ABI and tokenizer fingerprints before allowing automated fallback
Feature-flag coordinator per-org (default off) to avoid unexpected automation in older Dedicated/Private installs
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Kickoff meeting with Reliability, Runtime, and Console teams. Agreed on three-step state machine (detect -> isolate -> remediate).
2026-03-07: Prototype of routing API extension landed (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/route-coordinator/pull/418). Basic route-pin/unpin endpoints implemented.
2026-03-09: KV cache invalidation primitive added to runtime (feature-flagged) with initial TTL bump implementation (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2102).

2026-03-11: First integration test in staging: triggered automated fallback for synthetic regression against hosted model v2026-02; observed residual faulty outputs for tenant slice due to long-lived prefix caching. Identified need for explicit prefix-expire step.
2026-03-12: Added audit events for each coordinator action and pushed console stub for runbook view (console PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/997).
notes_and_findings: Sticky state comes in three flavors: KV per-token caches, prefix-embedding caches in Dedicated, and client-side pinned model handles. Each needs a different reconciliation action.
Private deployments require a smaller blast radius; we must expose a 'dry-run' mode that only emits planned actions without executing by default.
Observed latency spike when invalidating large prefix cache on gpu-hosted nodes; decide to stagger invalidation by shard to meet latency SLOs.
open_issues: Need a secure mechanism to run cache-invalidations in on-prem networks (work with Ops/Security to approve KMS keys for coordinator actions)
Define retention policy for coordinator audit logs to meet compliance for Private customers
Finalize tenant communication templates with CS and Legal for EU/UK data residency customers
next_steps: Implement prefix-expire primitive in runtime (engineers: Lina Xu, Rajesh Sangha) - estimate 3 points
Wire compatibility-check into coordinator API and block automated fallback if mismatch - owner: Marco Rivera
Add staged-invalidation orchestration to prevent SLO violations; add chaos test in staging - owner: Reliability team
Run full smoke regression with a set of 5 tenants (mix of hosted/dedicated/private) and produce roll-forward metrics dashboard
Schedule security review for Private coordinator agent (deadline 2026-03-16)
